title: The strict scalar identity unit is the Roos lift of scalar insertion
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l and a scheme X, with the coefficient constructions of [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models]. Let P be any ambient coefficient complex and C any strict quotient-system complex, with finite quotient identifications kappa_n. Suppose b maps the constant tower on P to the restricted tower C and has the section formula given by kappa_n inverse applied to 1 tensor x. Let q identify the restricted identity scalar extension of C with the specified scalar quotient tower on P, with the normalized tensor-generator formula of [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models]. Insert the scalar one using the inverse ordinary scalar unitor [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems], transpose b followed by this insertion through the ordinary constant/limit adjunction, and compose with the ordinary limit-to-Roos inclusion and Roos(q). The result equals the specified completedScalarIdentityUnit [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] as a chain map. This assertion has no derived realization model, adjunction calculus or completion comparison in its hypotheses or conclusion.

source.place: Tag 0941, sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok and the preceding constant/limit adjunction discussion in section-derived-limits, combined with the identity scalar tensor calculation in Bhatt--Scholze, Definition 3.4.10; agent expansion of scalar-model-unit proof steps 2--3.

proof.text: Multiplication of 1 tensor x is x by the ordinary scalar unitor normalization. Since multiplication is an isomorphism its inverse sends every x to 1 tensor x. The actual scalar-restriction functor preserves underlying sections and morphisms, with its specified cast identifications.

The counit formula for the ordinary adjunction shows that the nth component of the transpose is the nth component of b followed by scalar insertion. The section formulas for b and q therefore make the unshifted quotient components exactly 1 tensor x.

The limit-to-Roos inclusion has zero shifted component. Roos(q) acts diagonally on both product coordinates, so the composite also has zero shifted component. The defining coordinates of completedScalarIdentityUnit and product/biproduct extensionality identify the two chain maps.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0941; formal naturality and tensor-unit expansion of lem-trf-scalar-model-unit steps 2--3.

mathlib_searches.query: Scalar extension along identity multiplication inverse inserts one tensor a section and commutes with the inverse limit cone
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits, including ModuleCat.extendScalarsId_inv_app_apply and ModuleCat.extendScalarsId_hom_app_one_tmul. These compute ordinary module tensor insertion and multiplication, but do not identify the specified sheaf scalar tower, its section transports, or its Roos cone.
Found CochainComplex.mappingCocone.lift_fst; this supplies the first coordinate formula only.

theorem scalarIdentityRoosAugmentation
    (P : CochainComplex (scalarReductionSource l E X) ℤ)
    (C : CochainComplex (coefficientSequenceModules l E X) ℤ)
    (κ : ∀ n : ℕ,
      ((coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E X n).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj C ≅
        (unrestrictedIntegralFiniteComplex l E X n).obj P)
    (b : ((Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ : scalarReductionSource l E X ⥤
        ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ scalarReductionSource l E X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P ⟶
      ((coefficientSequenceRestriction l E X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj C)
    (hb : ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ) (U : X.ProEtᵒᵖ) (x : (P.X i).val.obj U),
      (((b.f i).app (op n)).val.app U) x =
        integralComparisonRestrictedSection l E X (C.X i) n U
          (integralComparisonSequenceSection l E X (C.X i) n U
            (((κ n).inv.f i).val.app U
              (unrestrictedIntegralTensorSection l E X n (P.X i) U 1 x))))
    (q : (((coefficientSequenceRestriction l E X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
        (((integralComparisonSequenceScalarModel l E E
          (AlgHom.id ℚ_[l] E) X).E.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj C)).asFunctor ≅
      (integralScalarTowerFunctor l E E (AlgHom.id ℚ_[l] E) X).obj P)
    (hq : ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ) (U : X.ProEtᵒᵖ)
        (s : (coefficientSequenceCommRingSheaf l E X).obj.obj (op (n, U.unop)))
        (x : (P.X i).val.obj U),
      ((q.hom.app (op n)).f i).val.app U
        (integralComparisonRestrictedSection l E X
          ((integralComparisonSequenceScalarModel l E E (AlgHom.id ℚ_[l] E) X).E.obj
            (C.X i)) n U
          (integralComparisonSequenceTensorSection l E E (AlgHom.id ℚ_[l] E) X
            (C.X i) (op (n, U.unop)) s
            (integralComparisonSequenceSection l E X (C.X i) n U
              (((κ n).inv.f i).val.app U
                (unrestrictedIntegralTensorSection l E X n (P.X i) U 1 x))))) =
        integralScalarTensorSection l E E (AlgHom.id ℚ_[l] E) X n (P.X i) U s x) :
    ((constLimAdj (J := ℕᵒᵖ) (C := scalarReductionSource l E X)).mapHomologicalComplex
        (.up ℤ)).homEquiv P _
      (b ≫ ((coefficientSequenceRestriction l E X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map
        ((NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex (integralComparisonSequenceScalarUnit l E X)
          (.up ℤ)).inv.app C)) ≫
      integralComparisonLimitToRoos l E X _ ≫
      integralOperationsRoosFunctor.map q.hom =
        (completedScalarIdentityUnit l E X).app P
